newsitem.title: USA: US automaker group says yen fall a serious problem.
newsitem.headline: US automaker group says yen fall a serious problem.

text.p: An automobile manufacturers' group on Wednesday decried the recent sharp fall in the Japanese yen versus the dollar, saying it could hurt the U.S. trade performance in the auto sector.

"The free fall of the yen is becoming a serious problem which is disrupting U.S. business planning and threatening many U.S. export opportunities," Andrew Card, president of the American Automobile Manufacturers Association, said in a statement.
"There is already clear evidence of the effects of the yen's excessive depreciation on U.S. trade performance in the automotive sector," said Card.

He cited a surge in Japan's auto exports to the United States in the latter part of 1996 following a decline in the early part of the year and said the increase resulted as the effects of the weak yen became visible.
He said the recent rise in the dollar above the key psychological level of 120 yen required the "immediate attention" of U.S. and Japanese officials.
